body.statement: If \(\delta_n\equiv\delta_0\in(0,\infty)\) and \(E_P[\phi_{\delta_0}(O)^2]\in(0,\infty)\), then the target and score reduce to Kennedy's point-treatment incremental mean and efficient influence function, and the Gaussian interval reduces to the pointwise version of Kennedy's fixed-compact multiplier procedure.
body.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check and prevents the hardening theory from changing the established estimand at ordinary multipliers.
body.gap: This is a compatibility corollary rather than a novelty claim; it pins the new notation to Kennedy2019Incremental exactly.
body.consumer: Existing bounded-multiplier analyses retain their familiar pointwise Gaussian interpretation.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(D_0(x)=1+(\delta_0-1)e(x)=\delta_0e(x)+1-e(x)\).  Because \(0<e(x)\leq 1\) and \(\delta_0>0\),
\[
D_0(x)=(1-e(x))\cdot 1+e(x)\delta_0\geq \min\{1,\delta_0\}>0.
\]
Thus every division below is well defined.  By \(\texttt{def:incremental-intervention}\) and \(\tau=\mu_1-\mu_0\), fixing \(\delta_n=\delta_0\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
m_{\delta_0}(x)
&=\mu_0(x)+\frac{\delta_0e(x)\{\mu_1(x)-\mu_0(x)\}}{D_0(x)}\\
&=\frac{D_0(x)\mu_0(x)+\delta_0e(x)\{\mu_1(x)-\mu_0(x)\}}{D_0(x)}\\
&=\frac{\delta_0e(x)\mu_1(x)+\{1-e(x)\}\mu_0(x)}{\delta_0e(x)+1-e(x)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Taking \(P\)-expectations and again using \(\texttt{def:incremental-intervention}\) yields
\[
\psi_{\delta_0}(P)
=E_P\!\left[
\frac{\delta_0e(X)\mu_1(X)+\{1-e(X)\}\mu_0(X)}
{\delta_0e(X)+1-e(X)}
\right].
\]
This is Kennedy's point-treatment incremental mean by \(\texttt{lem:kennedy-point-treatment-mean}\).  Notice that this is equality of the observed-law identifying functionals; it is not being imposed as a new definition of the causal target.

For the score comparison, let \(\varphi_a^{\mathrm K}\) denote the uncentered treatment-specific influence-function term in \(\texttt{lem:kennedy-point-treatment-eif}\).  Since \(e(X)>0\),
\[
e(X)\varphi_1^{\mathrm K}(O)
=A\{Y-\mu_1(X)\}+e(X)\mu_1(X).
\]
For \(e(X)<1\), similarly,
\[
\{1-e(X)\}\varphi_0^{\mathrm K}(O)
=(1-A)\{Y-\mu_0(X)\}+\{1-e(X)\}\mu_0(X).
\]
At \(e(X)=1\), the right-hand side of the latter display is zero \(P\)-almost surely because \(P(A=0\mid X)=1-e(X)=0\).  Hence that display supplies the almost-sure continuous-product interpretation required at the boundary, without division by \(1-e(X)\).  Substitution into Kennedy's efficient influence function gives, \(P\)-almost surely,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\phi^{\mathrm K}_{\delta_0}(O)
&=\frac{\delta_0e(X)\varphi_1^{\mathrm K}(O)+\{1-e(X)\}\varphi_0^{\mathrm K}(O)}{D_0(X)}
+\frac{\delta_0\tau(X)\{A-e(X)\}}{D_0(X)^2}-\psi_{\delta_0}(P)\\
&=\frac{A\delta_0\{Y-\mu_1(X)\}}{D_0(X)}
+\frac{(1-A)\{Y-\mu_0(X)\}}{D_0(X)}
+\frac{\delta_0e(X)\mu_1(X)+\{1-e(X)\}\mu_0(X)}{D_0(X)}\\
&\qquad+\frac{\delta_0\tau(X)\{A-e(X)\}}{D_0(X)^2}-\psi_{\delta_0}(P)\\
&=\frac{A\delta_0\{Y-\mu_1(X)\}}{D_0(X)}
+\frac{(1-A)\{Y-\mu_0(X)\}}{D_0(X)}
+\frac{\delta_0\tau(X)\{A-e(X)\}}{D_0(X)^2}
+m_{\delta_0}(X)-\psi_{\delta_0}(P)\\
&=\phi_{\delta_0}(O),
\end{aligned}
\]
where the penultimate equality uses the already proved identity for \(m_{\delta_0}\), and the last equality is exactly \(\texttt{def:oracle-score}\).  This proves equality with the cited efficient influence function, including the propensity-path term.

The variance premise now implies
\[
\sigma_0^2:=E_P\{\phi_{\delta_0}(O)^2\}
=E_P\{\phi^{\mathrm K}_{\delta_0}(O)^2\}\in(0,\infty),
\]
so the population standardization at the fixed multiplier is nondegenerate.  Moreover, the algebra above is pointwise in the nuisance functions.  Applying it fold by fold to the fitted nuisance functions in \(\texttt{def:local-linear-one-step}\) shows that each \(\widehat\varphi_{\delta_0,i}\) is the corresponding fitted uncentered Kennedy score.  Consequently its cross-fitted average \(\widehat\psi_{\delta_0}\) is Kennedy's sample-split point-treatment estimator, and \(\texttt{def:crossfit-score-variance}\) gives exactly the empirical centered score variance used in his pointwise procedure; these source-side constructions are recorded in \(\texttt{lem:kennedy-pointwise-gaussian-procedure}\).

Finally, substituting \(\delta_n=\delta_0\) in \(\texttt{def:branchwise-intervals}\) gives
\[
C_n^{\mathrm G}(\gamma)
=\left[
\widehat\psi_{\delta_0}
-z_{1-\gamma/2}\frac{\widehat\sigma_n}{\sqrt n},\;
\widehat\psi_{\delta_0}
+z_{1-\gamma/2}\frac{\widehat\sigma_n}{\sqrt n}
\right].
\]
This is the pointwise normal interval obtained by evaluating the fixed-compact multiplier procedure at \(\delta_0\); for \(\gamma=0.05\), its normal critical value is \(z_{0.975}\), conventionally rounded to \(1.96\), exactly as in the cited procedure.  This last assertion is a reduction of formulas only; no coverage claim is made here without the nuisance-rate hypotheses of the relevant Gaussian theorem.
